definitions.explanation: A person's family name, as opposed to their given name. In Japanese naming order, the surname comes first.

examples.japanese: {姓|せい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{名|めい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}いて→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please write your surname and given name.

examples.japanese: ⟦{結婚|けっこん}→結婚：02514_kekkon⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧{姓|せい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わった→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: My surname changed when I got married.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧{姓|せい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{名乗|なの}る→名乗る：11874_nanoru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{法律|ほうりつ}→法律：01722_houritsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{決|き}められている→決める：00858_kimeru⟧。
examples.english: In Japan, the law requires married couples to share the same surname.

notes:
USAGE:
{姓|せい} is a formal word for surname. In everyday speech, {名字|みょうじ} or ⟦{苗字|みょうじ}→苗字：14012_myouji⟧ is more common. {姓|せい} appears frequently on official forms and in formal writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {姓|せい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{名|めい} (surname and given name)
- {姓|せい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{名乗|なの}る→名乗る：11874_nanoru⟧ (to go by a surname)
- ⟦{旧姓|きゅうせい}→旧姓：12957_kyuusei⟧ (maiden name; former surname)
- ⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧{別姓|べっせい} (separate surnames for married couples)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{名字|みょうじ} is the everyday equivalent. {氏|し} is used in formal/legal contexts. {姓|せい} falls in between.
